subject: Can I make the plot box obey xlim and ylim exactly?

messages.author: 641d929e96c82906
messages.subject: Can I make the plot box obey xlim and ylim exactly?
parts:
It is a feature of R that plot boxes extend slightly outside the axis
limits. That also applies to the default grey background of ggplot:

qplot(0.5, 0.5) + xlim(0,1) + ylim(0,1) + coord_equal()
leaves lots of little grey rectangles outside the unit square.

I am plotting proportions and want to fix the limits at (0, 1) and
remove the gridlines. The grey box then gives a misleading impression
of how far the numbers are from the extremes. Can I force the box to
stay within limits?

opts(panel.background=theme_rect()) does not seem to offer any
arguments for this.

Any help appreciated.

Regards,
Jon Olav

messages.author: affa918ed63b6275
messages.subject: Re: Can I make the plot box obey xlim and ylim exactly?
parts:
hi,

is this what you want?

qplot(0:10/10,0:10/10)+opts(aspect.ratio=1)+coord_cartesian(xlim=c(0,1),ylim=c(0,1))+scale_x_continuous(breaks=c(0,1),
minor_breaks=NA)+scale_y_continuous(breaks=c(0,1),minor_breaks=NA)

HTH.

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Can I make the plot box obey xlim and ylim exactly?
parts:
It's probably better to set expand explicitly, rather than using
coordinate system limits:

qplot(0:10/10,0:10/10) +
scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0))

Hadley
